resources.string: Little gestures for the people you care about, on a cadence that never feels mechanical.
Add a reminder to nudge yourself to do the little things, like bringing flowers or calling to catch up.
Arrives every %1$d to %2$d days, varying each time, never on a fixed rhythm.
A novel, slightly challenging shared activity. Novelty renews closeness and passion.
A calm check-in on the week, opening with what you appreciate about each other.
Ask about their current worries, hopes and small news, so you never drift apart.
Plan casual face-to-face time. Shared hours are what turn a contact into a close friend.
Ask their opinion on a real decision. Being asked makes people feel valued and invested.
A regular adult-to-adult call keeps the bond warm without slipping into old dynamics.
A light, upbeat message or call. Siblings drift into apathy without active contact.
Offer and ask for help, so they feel useful, not merely cared for.

Relationships don\'t survive on inertia. They\'re subject to a constant emotional entropy and need active, intentional maintenance: small, regular gestures of attention. Research links weak social ties to health risks on a par with well-known clinical factors, so tending your closest bonds is among the highest-leverage things you can do.

A gesture that arrives like clockwork reads as automatic. The brain habituates to predictable rewards, and a reminder that fires on the same rhythm every time starts to feel like a chore rather than a genuine act of care. Novelty and a touch of unpredictability keep the same gesture feeling spontaneous, which is exactly what makes it land as authentic.

You set a rough cadence, for example \"about every two weeks.\" Each time a reminder fires, the app draws the next one at random from a window around your target, so \"every two weeks\" might actually be 12, 15 or 17 days. The rhythm never settles into a pattern, and the interval is measured from when you last acted, so it never drifts or piles up.

The presets draw on established relationship science: Gottman\'s rituals of connection and \"love maps,\" Aron\'s self-expansion model (novelty renews closeness), Gable\'s work on celebrating good news, and Hall\'s and Dunbar\'s findings on how time and contact sustain friendship.
